When Fanyu Meng started Ziyu Acoustics a few years ago, just as AirPods were taking off, two predictions were going around: if Apple moved into hearing aids, it would create yet another monopoly; or the hearing-aid market was too small for Apple to bother with. In September 2024 Apple answered, and he reposted audioXpress’s report in the original English.

A free software update turns AirPods Pro 2 (the models with the H2 chip) into an end-to-end hearing-health device. Hearing Protection, on by default, reduces loud, intermittent noise 48,000 times per second while keeping live music natural. A scientifically validated Hearing Test uses pure-tone audiometry and stores a personal hearing profile in the Health app. A clinical-grade, over-the-counter Hearing Aid feature for mild to moderate hearing loss uses that profile to boost the surrounding sound in real time, and also applies it to music, films and calls. The FDA authorized the feature only three days after the announcement.

The point, the article argues, is not extra sales but added value: reaching the many people with mild hearing loss who would never consider a hearing aid. The Apple Hearing Study, run with the University of Michigan and the World Health Organization, found that 75 percent of people diagnosed with hearing loss go untreated, and the WHO estimates that about 1.5 billion people have some degree of hearing loss. The features were due in fall 2024 in more than 100 countries and regions, on earbuds that sell for USD 249.

Reposted by Fanyu Meng from “Apple Announces AirPods Pro 2 Are Now Officially Hearing-Aids” by João Martins, published in audioXpress (September 2024). Read the original.
